(Jacksonville, Florida) | college = [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] (2014–2018) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | highlights = * [[List of NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Champions|NCAA champion]] ([[2015 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2015]]) * Second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[Sporting News|SN]] ([[2016 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2016]]) * Third-team All-American – [[Associated Press|AP]], [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] (2016) * First-team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] (2016) * Third-team All-ACC (2018) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald’s All-American]] ([[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2014]]) | medaltemplates = }} '''Grayson James Allen'''{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209693395 |title=Grayson Allen Bio - Duke University Blue Devils | Official Athletics Site |website=GoDuke.com |date= |accessdate=2017-03-20}} (born October 8, 1995) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Duke University]]. ==High school career== [[File:20140402 MCDAAG Grayson Allen dunk (2).JPG|thumb|right|Allen dunking in the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2014 McDonald's All-American Game]]]] In 2014, Allen was selected as a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] out of [[Providence School]] in [[Jacksonville, Florida]], where he won a state championship the previous year.{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24424133/players-announced-for-mcdonalds-all-american-game|title=Players announced for McDonald's All-American Game|accessdate=November 20, 2014|date=January 1, 2013|author=Borzello, Jeff|publisher=[[CBS Sports]]}} He won the McDonald's All-American Slam Dunk Contest, jumping over future Duke teammate [[Jahlil Okafor]].{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/highschool-prep-rally/grayson-allen-leaps-over-6-foot-10-jahlil-okafor-to-win-mcdonald-s-dunk-contest-183314008.html|title=Grayson Allen leaps over 6-foot-10 Jahlil Okafor to win McDonald's dunk contest|publisher=Yahoo! Sports|first=Ben|last=Rohrbach|date=April 2, 2014|accessdate=April 7, 2015}} ==College career== [[File:DUKEvUNC 2018-03-03 - Mike Krzyzewski hugs Grayson Allen 1.jpg|thumb|right|upright=1.4|[[Mike Krzyzewski|Coach K]] embraces Allen at the end of his final home game of his senior year at Duke University.]] During Allen's freshman season at Duke, he averaged 4.4 points per game{{cite web|title = Grayson Allen Bio|url = http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209693395|website = goduke.com|access-date = 2016-02-09}} and was named to the ACC all-academic team. Allen became a major contributor in the NCAA tournament. On April 7, 2015, he played in the [[2015 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game|championship game]], scoring 16 points, including 8 straight.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=400788981|title=Comeback! Duke dispatches Wisconsin to capture national title No. 5|work=ESPN|date=April 6, 2015|accessdate=April 7, 2015}} After the game, commentators cited Allen as one of the main reasons for Duke's win.{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2015/04/06/duke-wisconsin-national-championship-final-four-ncaa-tournament/25386447/|title=Duke edges Wisconsin to win fifth national championship|first=Paul|last=Myerberg|work=[[USA Today]]|date=April 7, 2015|accessdate=April 7, 2015}} Coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]] agreed, saying, "We were kind of dead in the water. We were nine points down and Grayson just put us on his back."{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/tourney/2015/04/06/duke-wisconsin-final-four-ncaa-tournament-championship-march-madnessgrayson-allen-tyus-jones-mike-krzyzewski/25386537/|title=Duke freshmen give Blue Devils late boost for title|first=Dan|last= Wolken|work=[[USA Today]]|date=April 7, 2015|accessdate=April 7, 2015}} During the 2015–16 season, Allen was one of the best offensive players in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]], averaging 21 points per game{{cite web|title=Atlantic Coast Conference Statistics - College Basketball - ESPN|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/conferences/statistics/player/_/id/2/acc-conference|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2016-02-09}} and shooting 43% from three-point range. He played an average of 36.6 minutes per game and made 83.7% of his free throws. {{cite web|title=Atlantic Coast Conference Statistics - College Basketball - ESPN|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/conferences/statistics/player/_/id/2/stat/scoring-per-game/sort/threePointFieldGoalPct/acc-conference|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2016-02-09}} Entering his junior season, Allen was considered one of the top returning players in college basketball. He was named to the [[Associated Press]] preseason All-America team{{cite news|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/duke-s-allen-leads-ap-preseason-all-america-team-110216 |title=Duke's Allen leads AP preseason All-America team |publisher=[[Foxsports.com]] |date=November 2, 2016 |accessdate=November 12, 2016}} and was the ACC media's pick as preseason ACC Player of the Year.{{cite news|first=Matt|last=Norlander |url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/duke-the-pick-to-win-a-loaded-acc-grayson-allen-is-preseason-player-of-the-year/ |title=Duke the pick to win a loaded ACC, Grayson Allen is preseason Player of the Year |publisher=[[CBSSports.com]] |date=October 26, 2016 |accessdate=November 12, 2016}} During the 2016–2017 season, Allen averaged 14.5 points per game and shot 36.5% from three-point range. He played on average 29.6 minutes per game and was 81.1% from the free-throw line. {{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/3135045/grayson-allen|title=Grayson Allen|website=ESPN.com}} ===Tripping incidents=== Allen received national publicity for intentionally tripping [[Louisville Cardinals basketball|Louisville]]'s Raymond Spalding on February 8, 2016; an ESPN.com article asked if he was "the next hated white Duke player."{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/14644805/grayson-allen-being-hated-white-player-duke-blue-devils |title=Grayson Allen and being a hated white player with the Duke Blue Devils |website=Espn.go.com |date=2016-02-09 |accessdate=2017-03-20}} In the second game against Louisville that season, he was elbowed in the head while scuffling for a ball on the ground{{cite web |url=https://mtc.cdn.vine.co/r/videos/4E34E16DF61312893722987765760_5a8a2bb1e03.5.0.3298839490801504692.mp4?versionId%3DF7LpAfI9q.GyvomDBptPlH_1Iw11cv0W |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2016-02-20 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160221101652/https://mtc.cdn.vine.co/r/videos/4E34E16DF61312893722987765760_5a8a2bb1e03.5.0.3298839490801504692.mp4?versionId=F7LpAfI9q.GyvomDBptPlH_1Iw11cv0W |archivedate=2016-02-21 |df= }} and later received a technical and ejection for yelling at a referee following his fifth foul on a charge call.{{cite web|author=Matt Brown |url=http://www.sportsonearth.com/article/165017632/duke-meltdown-issues-louisville-recap |title=A late meltdown at Louisville re-exposed Duke's issues. |publisher=Sports on Earth |date=2016-02-20 |accessdate=2017-03-20}} On Thursday, February 25, 2016, in the closing seconds of a 15-point win against FSU, Allen tripped FSU's [[Xavier Rathan-Mayes]].{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/14853209/grayson-allen-duke-blue-devils-suspended-acc-apparent-trip |title=Grayson Allen of Duke Blue Devils won't be suspended by ACC for apparent trip |website=Espn.go.com |date=2016-02-27 |accessdate=2017-03-20}} A day later, Allen received a reprimand from the ACC for his second tripping incident in less than a month. Prior to the start of his junior season, Allen stated that he was ready to put the tripping incidents behind him.{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/17823836/duke-blue-devils-grayson-allen-ready-put-tripping-incidents-him |title=Duke Blue Devils Grayson Allen ready to put tripping incidents behind him |website=Espn.com |date=2016-10-25 |accessdate=2017-03-20}} He then tripped the [[Elon Phoenix men's basketball|Elon]]'s Steven Santa Ana during their December 21 game. Allen was charged with a technical on the play.{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/video/clip/_/id/18328374 |title=Grayson Allen gets a tech for tripping again |website=Espn.com |date=2016-12-21 |accessdate=2017-03-20}}{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/video/clip?id=18328343 |title=Grayson Allen reacts to getting called for a Technical Foul after tripping a player |website=Espn.com |date=2016-12-21 |accessdate=2017-03-20}} The next day, Coach Krzyzewski suspended Allen from the team indefinitely and subsequently stripped him of his team captaincy after Duke's game on December 31.{{cite web |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/acc/2016/12/22/duke-mike-krzyzewski-suspends-grayson-allen-indefinitely/95742040/ |title=Duke's Mike Krzyzewski suspends Grayson Allen indefinitely |author=Nicole Auerbach |work=USA Today |date=2016-12-22 |accessdate=2016-12-22}}{{cite web |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2016/12/31/duke-grayson-allen-no-longer-team-captain |title=Duke’s Grayson Allen stripped of captaincy after suspension for tripping |work=Sports Illustrated |date=2016-12-31 |accessdate=2017-01-05}} Allen returned to play on January 4, 2017, after being suspended for one game.{{cite web |url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/grayson-allen-suspension-duke-kicking-mike-krzyzewski-coach-k-joke-indefinite-010417 |title=What a joke! Coach K ends Grayson Allen’s ‘indefinite suspension’ after just one game |author=Chris Chase |publisher=Fox Sports |date=2017-01-04 |accessdate=2017-01-05}} On March 9, 2018, Allen was assessed a flagrant foul 1 in the ACC tournament for tripping North Carolina's Garrison Brooks with what was euphemistically called a "hip check."{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/03/09/dukes-allen-gets-flagrant-1-for-hip-check-on-uncs-brooks/32800351/|title=Grayson Allen gets Flagrant 1 foul for hip check in ACC
